# MATTER LAB science API

<!-- Generated by services/science/scripts/build_api_reference.py. Do not edit by hand: change the script or the service and regenerate. -->

Reference for the science service, version 0.1.0. Base URL of the development stack: **`http://127.0.0.1:8787`** (`docker compose -p matterlab up -d`). Interactive documentation: `/docs`; machine-readable schema: `/openapi.json` (a copy is in [`openapi.json`](openapi.json)).

**How this file was made.** The endpoint list, parameters, request fields and status codes below are read from the service's OpenAPI schema. Every example is a real HTTP exchange, captured on 2026-11-14 from the service running on a freshly migrated and seeded database (schema version 0005; engines: RDKit 2026.09.2, xTB (tblite) 0.8.0, PySCF 2.15.0). Nothing in the examples was edited, with one exception that is always marked: long lists are cut to their first items followed by `"… N more"`, long texts end in `… (N characters)`, and in a few places a nested document is replaced by `"{… N fields}"` or `"[… N items]"`.

## Conventions

- **JSON everywhere.** Request and response bodies are JSON (the workbook export and upload excepted).
- **One error shape.** Every non-2xx response is `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": ...}}`. `code` is stable and machine-readable; `details` depends on the code (for `validation_error` it is a list of `{location, message, type}`). See [Errors](#errors).
- **Units.** Coordinates are in angstrom. Every numeric field carries its unit in its name (`energy_hartree`, `melting_point_k`, `molecular_weight_g_per_mol`) or in a `units`/`unit` field next to it.
- **Time.** Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Retrieval dates are ISO dates.
- **Nulls.** Every field of a response schema is present. A value that does not exist is `null`; fields are not omitted.
- **Identifiers.** Records have UUIDs. Catalogue compounds, solvents and catalysts have name-based (version 5) UUIDs derived from the InChIKey or the name, so the same record has the same id in every instance.
- **Provenance.** Every stored record has a source in the registry (`GET /v1/data-sources`). List responses carry `items[].source` (a key into the page's `sources` map); detail responses embed a `provenance` object with source, version, URL, retrieval date, licence (where the source states one) and citations. The object has the fields of the `Provenance` type of `packages/core` (`source`, `version`, `citations`, `url`, `retrieved`, `license`, `notes`) plus `source_key`, `kind` and `publisher`.
- **Evidence labels.** `reference` (taken from a published dataset or service), `computed` (calculated by an engine from the given input), `rule-based` (an empirical model or a pattern definition), `user-input` (typed in or imported; not verified by the service), `unsupported`, `illustrative` (never assigned by the service itself).
- **No invented results.** A structure RDKit rejects comes back with RDKit's own messages. A calculation an engine cannot do ends as `unsupported` or `failed` with the reason; such a job has no `result`. A search that finds nothing says which catalogue was searched, how many records it held and when, and nothing more.
- **CORS.** Allowed origins: `http://127.0.0.1:5273`, `http://localhost:5273`, `http://127.0.0.1:4273`, `http://localhost:4273` (setting `MATTERLAB_CORS_ORIGINS`).

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/` | Service information |
| `GET` | `/health` | Health of the service and its database |
| `GET` | `/v1/engines` | Scientific engines available in this instance |
| `POST` | `/v1/chem/validate` | Validate and normalise a structure |
| `POST` | `/v1/chem/3d` | Generate 3D coordinates |
| `POST` | `/v1/chem/descriptors` | Property-panel descriptors |
| `POST` | `/v1/chem/functional-groups` | Detect functional groups |
| `GET` | `/v1/job-kinds` | Job kinds and their input, settings and result schemas |
| `POST` | `/v1/jobs` | Submit a job |
| `GET` | `/v1/jobs` | List jobs, newest first |
| `GET` | `/v1/jobs/{job_id}` | Get a job with its progress, messages and result |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/jobs/{job_id}` | Cancel a job |
| `GET` | `/v1/data-sources` | Registered data sources (the provenance registry) |
| `GET` | `/v1/elements` | All chemical elements |
| `GET` | `/v1/elements/{element}` | One element with field-level provenance |
| `GET` | `/v1/isotopes` | Evaluated ground-state nuclides |
| `GET` | `/v1/functional-groups/sets` | Functional-group definition sets |
| `GET` | `/v1/functional-groups` | Functional-group definitions (SMARTS) |
| `GET` | `/v1/solvents` | Common solvents |
| `GET` | `/v1/solvents/{solvent_id}` | One solvent |
| `GET` | `/v1/catalysts` | Common catalysts |
| `GET` | `/v1/catalysts/{catalyst_id}` | One catalyst |
| `GET` | `/v1/compounds` | List or look up compounds |
| `POST` | `/v1/compounds/search/exact` | Exact structure lookup |
| `POST` | `/v1/compounds/search/substructure` | Substructure search |
| `POST` | `/v1/compounds/search/similarity` | Similarity search |
| `GET` | `/v1/compounds/{compound_id}` | One compound with structure, names and provenance |
| `POST` | `/v1/reactions` | Create a reaction |
| `GET` | `/v1/reactions` | List reactions |
| `GET` | `/v1/reactions/{reaction_id}` | One reaction with its participants |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/reactions/{reaction_id}` | Delete a reaction |
| `POST` | `/v1/experiments` | Save a new experiment |
| `GET` | `/v1/experiments` | List experiments, most recently updated first |
| `GET` | `/v1/experiments/{experiment_id}` | Reopen an experiment |
| `PUT` | `/v1/experiments/{experiment_id}` | Replace an experiment |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/experiments/{experiment_id}` | Change some fields of an experiment |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/experiments/{experiment_id}` | Delete an experiment |
| `POST` | `/v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/rerun` | Reproduce an experiment by repeating its calculations |
| `POST` | `/v1/discoveries` | Create a discovery candidate from a structure |
| `GET` | `/v1/discoveries` | List discovery candidates, most recently updated first |
| `GET` | `/v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}` | One candidate with searches and evidence |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}` | Change the title or notes |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}` | Delete a candidate with its searches and evidence |
| `POST` | `/v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}/searches` | Search the catalogues again |
| `POST` | `/v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}/evidence` | Attach evidence |
| `POST` | `/v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}/status` | Move a candidate on the status ladder |
| `GET` | `/v1/excel/format` | The workbook format: sheets, headers, types and units |
| `GET` | `/v1/excel/export` | Download the database as an .xlsx workbook |
| `POST` | `/v1/excel/import` | Import an .xlsx workbook |

## Service

### `GET /`

**Service information.**

Responses: `200` `ServiceInfo`.

```http
GET /
```

`HTTP 200`
```json
{
  "service": "matterlab-science",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "MATTER LAB science service: validated scientific libraries behind a typed HTTP API.",
  "api_base": "/v1",
  "docs": "/docs",
  "openapi": "/openapi.json",
  "health": "/health"
}
```

### `GET /health`

**Health of the service and its database.** 200 when the service can reach PostgreSQL and its schema is in place; 503 otherwise.

### `GET /v1/engines`

**Scientific engines available in this instance.** Engines are detected at start-up by importing them and running a small real calculation. Versions are read from the installed libraries, never hard-coded.

Responses: `200` `EnginesResponse`.

An engine is listed as available only after it has been imported and has completed a small real calculation in this instance (`self_test`). Job kinds of an engine that is not available answer with status `unsupported`.

## Chemistry (synchronous, RDKit)

A structure is always given as `{"format": "smiles" | "molblock", "data": "..."}`.

### `POST /v1/chem/validate`

**Validate and normalise a structure.** Parses and sanitises the structure with RDKit. An invalid structure is a normal answer (`valid: false`, HTTP 200) carrying RDKit's own error messages and the atoms they refer to.

Request body (`application/json`): `ValidateRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `structure` | StructureInput | yes |  |  |
| `implicit_hydrogens` | boolean | no | `true` | True (default): standard valence model, missing hydrogens are implied. False (molblock only): the drawn atoms are the whole structure, no hydrogens are implied, and open valences are reported as radical electrons. |

Responses: `200` `ValidationResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`.

*Benzene*

```http
POST /v1/chem/validate
{"structure": {"format": "smiles", "data": "c1ccccc1"}}
```

### `POST /v1/chem/3d`

**Generate 3D coordinates.** ETKDGv3 embedding with explicit hydrogens, followed by MMFF94 (or UFF) clean-up. Coordinates of the input, if any, are not used. Atoms keep the input order; added hydrogens come last.

Request body (`application/json`): `Embed3DRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `structure` | StructureInput | yes |  |  |
| `random_seed` | integer | no | `61453` | Seed of the ETKDG embedding; the same seed reproduces the same coordinates. |
| `force_field` | `auto` \| `mmff94` \| `mmff94s` \| `uff` \| `none` | no | `"auto"` | Clean-up after embedding. `auto`: MMFF94, or UFF when MMFF94 has no parameters. `none`: return the raw ETKDG coordinates. |
| `max_iterations` | integer | no | `500` | Iteration limit of the force-field clean-up. |

Responses: `200` `Embed3DResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`.

*Ethanol*

```http
POST /v1/chem/3d
{"structure": {"format": "smiles", "data": "CCO"}}
```

### `POST /v1/chem/descriptors`

**Property-panel descriptors.** Descriptors computed by RDKit. Each value states its unit, its method and whether it is an estimate.

Request body (`application/json`): `DescriptorsRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `structure` | StructureInput | yes |  |  |

Responses: `200` `DescriptorsResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`.

*Aspirin*

```http
POST /v1/chem/descriptors
{"structure": {"format": "smiles", "data": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"}}
```

`HTTP 200`

### `POST /v1/chem/functional-groups`

**Detect functional groups.** Matches the SMARTS definitions stored in PostgreSQL (seeded from RDKit's own data files) against the structure. Names and patterns are RDKit's; the result is rule-based.

Request body (`application/json`): `FunctionalGroupsRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `structure` | StructureInput | yes |  |  |
| `sets` | array of string \| null | no |  | Definition sets to search; all sets when omitted. See GET /v1/functional-groups/sets. |

Responses: `200` `FunctionalGroupsResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

*Aspirin against one of the three definition sets*

```http
POST /v1/chem/functional-groups
{"structure": {"format": "smiles", "data": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"}, "sets": ["rdkit-functional-group-hierarchy"]}
```

## Jobs (asynchronous calculations)

A job is accepted with `202` and runs in a worker process of its own, so the API stays responsive. Poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` until `status` is terminal. Statuses: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `unsupported`. Every job is a row of the `calculations` table and keeps its kind, input, settings (with defaults filled in), `input_hash`, engine and versions, timestamps, messages, and its result or error.

`input_hash` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) of `{kind, input, settings}` after defaults have been applied; `timeout_seconds` is not part of it. The same request always has the same hash, so earlier runs can be found with `GET /v1/jobs?input_hash=...`.

`DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}` cancels: a queued job at once, a running job by terminating its worker process (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 3 s). A job that exceeds its time limit, or whose worker dies, ends as `failed` with error code `timeout` or `worker_crashed`.

### `GET /v1/job-kinds`

**Job kinds and their input, settings and result schemas.**

Responses: `200` `JobKindsResponse`.

| Kind | Engine | Available here | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rdkit.geometry_optimization` | rdkit | yes | Minimises a geometry with MMFF94 (or UFF when MMFF94 has no parameters) and returns the optimised coordinates, energies before and after, and convergence. |
| `rdkit.conformer_search` | rdkit | yes | Embeds conformers with ETKDGv3, minimises them with a force field, removes duplicates and returns the lowest-energy ones. |
| `xtb.single_point` | xtb | yes | Semi-empirical tight-binding energy, partial charges, dipole, orbital energies and bond orders at a fixed geometry. |
| `xtb.geometry_optimization` | xtb | yes | Optimises a geometry on the GFN-xTB potential energy surface with ASE's LBFGS optimiser. |
| `pyscf.single_point` | pyscf | yes | Self-consistent-field energy, orbital energies, Mulliken charges and dipole moment with a selectable basis set and functional. |

Settings of `rdkit.geometry_optimization`:

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `force_field` | `auto` \| `mmff94` \| `mmff94s` \| `uff` | `"auto"` | `auto` uses MMFF94 and falls back to UFF when MMFF94 has no parameters for the molecule. |
| `max_iterations` | integer | `2000` | Upper limit on minimiser iterations. |
| `random_seed` | integer | `61453` | Seed for ETKDG, used only when a starting geometry has to be generated. |
| `record_trajectory` | boolean | `false` | Return intermediate geometries and energies, and the exact iteration count. RDKit exposes neither, so the minimisation is replayed once per frame; expect roughly trajectory_max_frames / 2 times the cost of a plain optimisation. |
| `trajectory_stride` | integer | `1` | Minimum number of minimiser iterations between recorded frames. |
| `trajectory_max_frames` | integer | `30` | Upper limit on recorded frames; the stride is widened as needed to respect it. |

Settings of `rdkit.conformer_search`:

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `num_conformers` | integer | `50` | Number of conformers to embed. |
| `force_field` | `auto` \| `mmff94` \| `mmff94s` \| `uff` \| `none` | `"auto"` | Force field used to minimise and rank conformers; `none` returns the raw ETKDG conformers unranked. |
| `max_iterations` | integer | `500` | Minimiser iteration limit per conformer. |
| `random_seed` | integer | `61453` |  |
| `prune_rms_threshold_angstrom` | number | `0.5` | Minimised conformers closer than this heavy-atom RMSD (after alignment) to a lower-energy one are dropped. |
| `energy_window_kcal_per_mol` | number \| null | `null` | When set, conformers more than this far above the lowest energy are dropped. |
| `max_returned` | integer | `10` | Return at most this many conformers, lowest energy first. |

Settings of `xtb.single_point`:

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `GFN2-xTB` \| `GFN1-xTB` | `"GFN2-xTB"` |  |
| `accuracy` | number | `1.0` | tblite numerical accuracy factor for the self-consistent cycle (1.0 is the default; smaller is tighter). |
| `max_scf_iterations` | integer | `250` |  |
| `electronic_temperature_k` | number | `300.0` | Electronic temperature for Fermi smearing, in kelvin. |
| `random_seed` | integer | `61453` | Seed for ETKDG, used only when a geometry has to be generated. |

Settings of `xtb.geometry_optimization`:

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `GFN2-xTB` \| `GFN1-xTB` | `"GFN2-xTB"` |  |
| `accuracy` | number | `1.0` | tblite numerical accuracy factor for the self-consistent cycle (1.0 is the default; smaller is tighter). |
| `max_scf_iterations` | integer | `250` |  |
| `electronic_temperature_k` | number | `300.0` | Electronic temperature for Fermi smearing, in kelvin. |
| `random_seed` | integer | `61453` | Seed for ETKDG, used only when a geometry has to be generated. |
| `max_steps` | integer | `500` | Upper limit on optimiser steps. |
| `force_tolerance_ev_per_angstrom` | number | `0.05` | Converged when the largest atomic force falls below this value. |
| `record_trajectory` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `trajectory_max_frames` | integer | `200` |  |

Settings of `pyscf.single_point`:

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `hf` \| `dft` | `"hf"` | `hf` for Hartree-Fock, `dft` for Kohn-Sham DFT. |
| `functional` | string \| null | `null` | Exchange-correlation functional for `dft`, by its libxc/PySCF name (e.g. `b3lyp`, `pbe`, `pbe0`). Defaults to `b3lyp` for `dft`; must be omitted for `hf`. |
| `basis` | string | `"sto-3g"` | Gaussian basis set by its PySCF name, e.g. `sto-3g`, `6-31g*`, `def2-svp`, `cc-pvdz`. |
| `max_scf_cycles` | integer | `100` |  |
| `convergence_tolerance_hartree` | number | `1e-09` | SCF energy convergence threshold. |
| `grid_level` | integer | `3` | PySCF DFT integration grid level (used by `dft` only). |
| `random_seed` | integer | `61453` | Seed for ETKDG, used only when a geometry has to be generated. |

Input of the `rdkit.*` kinds: `{"structure": {format, data}}` (coordinates in a molblock are used as the starting geometry). Input of the `xtb.*` and `pyscf.*` kinds: `{"structure": ..., "charge": int, "multiplicity": int}`, where the structure may also be `{"format": "atoms", "atoms": [{"element", "x", "y", "z"}]}` with coordinates in angstrom. The full schemas, including the result of every kind, are in the response of `GET /v1/job-kinds`.

```http
GET /v1/job-kinds
```

`HTTP 200`
```json
{
  "kinds": [
    {
      "kind": "rdkit.geometry_optimization",
      "title": "Force-field geometry optimisation (RDKit)",
```

### `POST /v1/jobs`

**Submit a job.** Accepts a calculation and returns at once. The job runs in a separate worker process; poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` until the status is terminal (`succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `unsupported`). When the engine for the kind is not available in this instance the job is stored with status `unsupported` and the reasons, and is never run.

Request body (`application/json`): `RdkitGeometryOptimizationRequest | RdkitConformerSearchRequest | XtbSinglePointRequest | XtbGeometryOptimizationRequest | PyscfSinglePointRequest`

One of: `RdkitGeometryOptimizationRequest`, `RdkitConformerSearchRequest`, `XtbSinglePointRequest`, `XtbGeometryOptimizationRequest`, `PyscfSinglePointRequest` (selected by `kind`).

Responses: `202` `Job`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

*Submit: MMFF94 geometry optimisation of ethanol*

```http
POST /v1/jobs
{"kind": "rdkit.geometry_optimization", "input": {"structure": {"format": "smiles", "data": "CCO"}}}
```

### `DELETE /v1/jobs/{job_id}`

**Cancel a job.** Cancels a queued job immediately. For a running job the worker process is terminated (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL); the response still shows `running` with `cancel_requested: true` until the supervisor has confirmed the process is gone, then the status becomes `cancelled`. A job that is already terminal is returned unchanged. The record itself is kept.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |  |

Responses: `200` `Job`; `404` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

### `GET /v1/jobs`

**List jobs, newest first.**

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | query | `queued` \| `running` \| `succeeded` \| `failed` \| `cancelled` \| `unsupported` \| null | no |  | Only jobs in this status. |
| `kind` | query | string \| null | no |  | Only jobs of this kind. |
| `input_hash` | query | string \| null | no |  | Only jobs with this request hash (earlier runs of the same request). |
| `limit` | query | integer | no | `50` |  |
| `offset` | query | integer | no | `0` |  |

Responses: `200` `Page_JobSummary_`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

*All runs of one request*

Solvents and catalysts hold names, identifiers and structures only. The single stored property is the molecular weight that PubChem returned, kept together with its source. No boiling points, polarities or similar numbers are stored, because none were retrieved from a citable source.

## Compound catalogue and search

The catalogue is a starter set of common compounds retrieved from PubChem (see `services/science/seed/pubchem/snapshot.json`). Canonical SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, formula, masses and fingerprints are computed by RDKit from the structure PubChem returned.

**Where the searches run.** Exact lookups by InChIKey, name, formula or CID are answered by PostgreSQL from stored columns. Substructure and similarity searches run *in the science service* with RDKit, on the catalogue rows (structures and stored fingerprints) loaded from PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL has no chemistry cartridge in this stack. Every search response has a `scope` that states the catalogue, the number of records searched, the time and the method.

### `GET /v1/compounds`

**List or look up compounds.** Filters combine with AND. All matching is done by PostgreSQL on stored values.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inchikey` | query | string \| null | no |  | Exact standard InChIKey. |
| `name` | query | string \| null | no |  | Exact name, case-insensitive: preferred name, IUPAC name or a stored synonym. |
| `formula` | query | string \| null | no |  | Exact molecular formula. Element order does not matter (it is rewritten in Hill notation). |
| `pubchem_cid` | query | integer \| null | no |  | PubChem compound identifier. |
| `q` | query | string \| null | no |  | Case-insensitive fragment of a name or synonym. |
| `limit` | query | integer | no | `50` |  |
| `offset` | query | integer | no | `0` |  |

Responses: `200` `SourcedPage_CompoundListItem_`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

```http
GET /v1/compounds?name=aspirin
```

### `POST /v1/compounds/search/similarity`

**Similarity search.** Fingerprint similarity is a structural heuristic, not a statement about properties or activity.

Request body (`application/json`): `SimilaritySearchRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `structure` | StructureInput | yes |  |  |
| `threshold` | number | no | `0.7` | Minimum Tanimoto similarity. |
| `limit` | integer | no | `20` |  |

Responses: `200` `SimilaritySearchResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

*Neighbours of aspirin*

```http
POST /v1/compounds/search/similarity
{"structure": {"format": "smiles", "data": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"}, "threshold": 0.4, "limit": 3}
```

`HTTP 200`
```json
{
  "query": {
```

## Reactions

A reaction is stored as a reaction SMILES that RDKit has parsed. The service checks the atom balance and records it; it does not predict products, yields or rates.

### `POST /v1/reactions`

**Create a reaction.** The reaction SMILES is parsed by RDKit; every species is canonicalised, linked to the catalogue when its InChIKey is known there, and the element and charge balance is computed. The record is stored as user input: the service checks its chemistry, not whether it occurs.

Request body (`application/json`): `ReactionCreate`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  |  |
| `reaction_smiles` | string | yes |  | `reactants>agents>products`; repeat a species to give it a stoichiometric coefficient above 1. |
| `description` | string \| null | no |  |  |
| `temperature_k` | number \| null | no |  | Reaction temperature in kelvin. |
| `pressure_pa` | number \| null | no |  | Reaction pressure in pascal. |
| `solvent_id` | string (uuid) \| null | no |  |  |
| `catalyst_id` | string (uuid) \| null | no |  |  |
| `conditions` | object | no |  | Free-form additional conditions. |

Responses: `201` `Reaction`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

```http
POST /v1/reactions
{"name": "Hydrogenation of ethene", "reaction_smiles": "C=C.[H][H]>>CC", "temperature_k": 298.15}
```

## Experiments

An experiment stores what the client needs to reopen a piece of work: `inputs`, `settings` and `results` are client-defined JSON documents kept verbatim, and `calculation_ids` links jobs. Computed results stay in the jobs. `revision` increases with every change; pass `expected_revision` to refuse a lost update (409).

### `POST /v1/experiments`

**Save a new experiment.**

Request body (`application/json`): `ExperimentWrite`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | yes |  |  |
| `description` | string \| null | no |  |  |
| `kind` | string \| null | no |  | Free-form category chosen by the client. |
| `inputs` | object | no |  | Everything needed to rebuild the experiment (structures, scene, parameters). Stored verbatim as JSON. |
| `settings` | object | no |  | Client settings. Stored verbatim as JSON. |
| `results` | object | no |  | Client-side results. Computed results belong to the linked calculations. Stored verbatim as JSON. |
| `notes` | string \| null | no |  |  |
| `tags` | array of string | no |  |  |
| `reaction_id` | string (uuid) \| null | no |  |  |
| `calculation_ids` | array of string (uuid) | no |  | Jobs that belong to this experiment, in order. |

Responses: `201` `Experiment`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

```http
POST /v1/experiments
{"title": "Ethanol geometry", "kind": "molecule", "inputs": {"structure": {"format": "smiles", "data": "CCO"}}, "settings": {"force_field": "auto"}, "tags": ["demo"], "reaction_id": "4526e24b-6e9d-44ca-bbce-cb840d27cc9e", "calculation_ids": ["ef3a347a-21b8-4b2b-b1f0-e4b32b445df5"]}
```

*A stale revision is refused*

```http
PATCH /v1/experiments/3af1ff60-a440-460a-8128-937ed3df4f7a
{"notes": "A second writer with a stale copy", "expected_revision": 1}
```

`HTTP 409`
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "revision_conflict",
    "message": "The experiment is at revision 2, not 1; it was changed since you loaded it.",
    "details": {
      "current_revision": 2,
      "expected_revision": 1
    }
  }
}
```

### `PUT /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}`

**Replace an experiment.** Every field is replaced by the request (omitted fields return to their defaults).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `experiment_id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |  |

Request body (`application/json`): `ExperimentReplace`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | yes |  |  |
| `description` | string \| null | no |  |  |
| `kind` | string \| null | no |  | Free-form category chosen by the client. |
| `inputs` | object | no |  | Everything needed to rebuild the experiment (structures, scene, parameters). Stored verbatim as JSON. |
| `settings` | object | no |  | Client settings. Stored verbatim as JSON. |
| `results` | object | no |  | Client-side results. Computed results belong to the linked calculations. Stored verbatim as JSON. |
| `notes` | string \| null | no |  |  |
| `tags` | array of string | no |  |  |
| `reaction_id` | string (uuid) \| null | no |  |  |
| `calculation_ids` | array of string (uuid) | no |  | Jobs that belong to this experiment, in order. |
| `expected_revision` | integer \| null | no |  | When given, the update is refused with 409 unless the stored revision matches. |

Responses: `200` `Experiment`; `404` `ErrorResponse`; `409` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

### `POST /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/rerun`

**Reproduce an experiment by repeating its calculations.** Submits a new job for every calculation linked to the experiment, with exactly the stored kind, input and settings, and links the new jobs to the experiment. Because the request is identical the new job has the same `input_hash`; compare the two results to check reproducibility. Engine versions may differ from the original run and are recorded on each job.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `experiment_id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |  |

Responses: `202` `RerunResponse`; `404` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

### `DELETE /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}`

**Delete an experiment.** Removes the experiment and its links. The linked calculations themselves are kept.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `experiment_id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |  |

Responses: `204` no body; `404` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

Answers `204` without a body. The linked calculations are kept.

## Discovery candidates

A candidate is a structure a user proposes. The service normalises it with RDKit, searches the local catalogue (exact InChIKey and Morgan/Tanimoto similarity) and, only when asked with `query_pubchem: true`, asks PubChem for the InChIKey. Every step is written to an append-only evidence trail.

The status ladder, in order: `user-created`, `structurally-validated`, `no-match-in-searched-catalogs`, `computationally-plausible`, `experimentally-observed`, `independently-validated`. The service sets the first three. The later rungs are requested by the user, one at a time, and each needs its evidence: a succeeded, converged calculation on the same structure; an experimental observation with a reference; an independent validation with a reference. The service records user evidence as asserted by the user and does not verify it.

**What `no-match-in-searched-catalogs` means.** Exactly what it says: the catalogues listed in `searched_catalogs` had no record with this InChIKey at the stated times. `searched_catalogs` always names each catalogue, the number of records searched (when the catalogue reports it) and when. No response describes a candidate as new or previously unknown; an absent match is not evidence of that. A failed external lookup is recorded as `error` and does not count as a search. A later match in any catalogue returns the candidate to `structurally-validated`.

### `POST /v1/discoveries`

**Create a discovery candidate from a structure.** The service validates the structure with RDKit, searches the local catalogue (exact InChIKey and Morgan/Tanimoto similarity) and, only when `query_pubchem` is true, asks PubChem for the InChIKey. Each step is written to the evidence trail. An invalid structure is still stored (status `user-created`) together with RDKit's messages.

Request body (`application/json`): `DiscoveryCreate`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `similarity_threshold` | number | no | `0.7` | Minimum Tanimoto similarity for the local similarity search. |
| `similarity_limit` | integer | no | `10` |  |
| `query_pubchem` | boolean | no | `false` | Also ask PubChem (one PUG REST request) whether it has a compound with this InChIKey. The lookup, its time and its outcome are recorded. |
| `title` | string | yes |  |  |
| `structure` | StructureInput | yes |  |  |
| `notes` | string \| null | no |  |  |

Responses: `201` `Discovery`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

*A structure that is not in the local catalogue*

```http
POST /v1/discoveries
{"title": "Candidate A", "structure": {"format": "smiles", "data": "OC(=O)C1CC1c1ccncc1"}}
```

### `POST /v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}/searches`

**Search the catalogues again.** Repeats the local searches (the catalogue may have changed) and optionally the PubChem lookup. The new searches are added to the trail; the status follows what they find: an identical structure in any searched catalogue returns the candidate to `structurally-validated`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `discovery_id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |  |

Request body (`application/json`): `SearchRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `similarity_threshold` | number | no | `0.7` | Minimum Tanimoto similarity for the local similarity search. |
| `similarity_limit` | integer | no | `10` |  |
| `query_pubchem` | boolean | no | `false` | Also ask PubChem (one PUG REST request) whether it has a compound with this InChIKey. The lookup, its time and its outcome are recorded. |

Responses: `200` `Discovery`; `404` `ErrorResponse`; `409` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

With `{"query_pubchem": true}` the service sends one request to PubChem PUG REST (`/compound/inchikey/<key>/cids/JSON`) and records the request URL, the time, the HTTP status and the outcome. The example below repeats the local searches only.

```http
POST /v1/discoveries/e45c6aac-06dc-4459-8a91-f326c535d6fc/searches
{}
```

### `POST /v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}/evidence`

**Attach evidence.** Adds a record to the evidence trail: a calculation (an existing job), an experimental observation, an independent validation or a note. Observations and validations are recorded as asserted by the user; the service does not verify them. Attaching evidence never changes the status by itself; request a status change explicitly.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `discovery_id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |  |

Request body (`application/json`): `EvidenceCreate`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `calculation` \| `experimental-observation` \| `independent-validation` \| `note` | yes |  |  |
| `summary` | string \| null | no |  | What the evidence shows. Generated for `calculation`; required otherwise. |
| `calculation_id` | string (uuid) \| null | no |  | The job to attach (kind `calculation`). |
| `reference` | string \| null | no |  | Citation, DOI, URL or lab-notebook reference. Required for observations and validations. |
| `details` | object | no |  |  |

Responses: `201` `Discovery`; `404` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

*Attach a finished calculation*

```http
POST /v1/discoveries/e45c6aac-06dc-4459-8a91-f326c535d6fc/evidence
{"kind": "calculation", "calculation_id": "e87ba128-1481-4271-a12f-6639bc6072ca"}
```

### `POST /v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}/status`

**Move a candidate on the status ladder.** The ladder is climbed one rung at a time and each rung needs its evidence: `computationally-plausible` needs an attached calculation that succeeded, converged and was run on the candidate's structure (and no identical structure in the searched catalogues); `experimentally-observed` and `independently-validated` need the matching evidence record with a reference. `structurally-validated` and `no-match-in-searched-catalogs` are set only by the service. A status can be lowered, but not below what validation and the searches established. A refused transition answers 409 and says what is missing.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `discovery_id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |  |

Request body (`application/json`): `StatusChange`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `user-created` \| `structurally-validated` \| `no-match-in-searched-catalogs` \| `computationally-plausible` \| `experimentally-observed` \| `independently-validated` | yes |  |  |
| `justification` | string | yes |  |  |

Responses: `200` `Discovery`; `404` `ErrorResponse`; `409` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

*Rungs cannot be skipped*

```http
POST /v1/discoveries/e45c6aac-06dc-4459-8a91-f326c535d6fc/status
{"status": "independently-validated", "justification": "skipping ahead"}
```

`HTTP 409`
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "status_transition_not_allowed",
    "message": "The ladder is climbed one rung at a time; the next rung after 'no-match-in-searched-catalogs' is 'computationally-plausible'.",
    "details": {
      "current_status": "no-match-in-searched-catalogs",
      "requested_status": "independently-validated",
      "next_status": "computationally-plausible"
    }
  }
}
```

*One rung up, backed by the attached calculation*

```http
POST /v1/discoveries/e45c6aac-06dc-4459-8a91-f326c535d6fc/status
{"status": "computationally-plausible", "justification": "MMFF94 optimisation converged"}
```

### `PATCH /v1/discoveries/{discovery_id}`

**Change the title or notes.** The structure of a candidate cannot be changed: its searches and evidence refer to it. Create a new candidate instead.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `discovery_id` | path | string (uuid) | yes |  |  |

Request body (`application/json`): `DiscoveryPatch`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string \| null | no |  |  |
| `notes` | string \| null | no |  |  |

Responses: `200` `Discovery`; `404` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

## Excel

PostgreSQL is the authoritative store; a workbook is an interchange copy. The export has exactly ten worksheets, in this order: Elements, Isotopes, Compounds, Functional Groups, Catalysts, Solvents, Reactions, Experiments, Discoveries, Calculations. Units are part of the header text (`Atomic mass (u)`), every row ends with six provenance columns, and export time, schema version and service version are written to the workbook's document properties (and repeated in the response headers).

Import rules:
- Sheet names and headers are checked first. An unknown sheet, an unknown column, or a header in another unit (`Melting point (C)`) rejects the whole workbook (422 `workbook_rejected`); nothing is written.
- A workbook may contain any subset of the ten sheets. Read-only columns (derived values such as InChI or formula) may be left out; they are recomputed by RDKit and never trusted.
- Rows are validated one by one: cell types, required values, references, and chemistry (RDKit parses every SMILES, SMARTS and reaction SMILES). Invalid rows are listed with sheet, row, column, code and message; valid rows are applied.
- Everything happens in one transaction, and what a row writes is written inside its own savepoint. `atomic=true` writes nothing unless every row is valid; `dry_run=true` never writes.
- A row that is identical to the database is left untouched and keeps its provenance. Numbers are compared to a relative tolerance of 1e-14, because a worksheet cell stores 16 significant digits.
- A new or changed row gets the workbook as its provenance (file name, SHA-256, time) together with the source named in the row's `Source` columns, recorded as declared and not verified. Such records are labelled `user-input`.
- Calculations cannot be changed by import, and a finished calculation is accepted only if its input hash matches its kind, input and settings. The status, structure, searches and evidence of an existing discovery candidate cannot be changed by import.
- A cell holds at most 32,767 characters. On export a longer value is left out and its header is listed in `Omitted fields`; on import such a field keeps its stored value, and a record that does not exist yet is refused (`omitted_field`) rather than stored incomplete.
- Every import, applied or not, is logged in the `data_imports` table.

### `GET /v1/excel/export`

**Download the database as an .xlsx workbook.** Exactly ten worksheets, in this order: Elements, Isotopes, Compounds, Functional Groups, Catalysts, Solvents, Reactions, Experiments, Discoveries, Calculations. Units are in the headers and every row ends with its provenance. Export time and schema version are stored in the workbook's document properties and repeated in the response headers.

Responses: `200` `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

### `POST /v1/excel/import`

**Import an .xlsx workbook.** Sheet names, headers (units included), cell types, references and chemistry are validated. Valid rows are upserted with provenance and invalid rows are listed with sheet, row, column and reason. All writes happen in one transaction with a savepoint per row. A workbook with an unknown sheet or a wrong header is rejected as a whole (HTTP 422, with the report in `details`).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | query | boolean | no | `false` | Validate against the database and report what would happen; write nothing. |
| `atomic` | query | boolean | no | `false` | Write nothing unless every row is valid. |

Request body (`multipart/form-data`): one part named `file` holding the workbook.

Responses: `200` `ImportReport`; `413` `ErrorResponse`; `422` `ErrorResponse`; `503` `ErrorResponse`.

## Errors

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | The path or the record does not exist. |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` | The path exists but not with this method. |
| 409 | `revision_conflict, status_transition_not_allowed, structure_not_valid` | The request conflicts with the state of the record. `details` holds the current state. |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | An uploaded workbook exceeds `MATTERLAB_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`. |
| 422 | `validation_error` | The request does not match the schema. `details` lists `{location, message, type}`. |
| 422 | `invalid_structure` | RDKit could not interpret the structure. `message` and `details.errors` carry RDKit's own messages and the atoms concerned. |
| 422 | `invalid_query, invalid_reaction, structure_too_large, unknown_reference, unknown_functional_group_set, no_inchikey, external_lookups_disabled, empty_upload, workbook_rejected` | Other well-formed requests that cannot be carried out; the message says why. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | An unexpected failure. It is logged; the response carries only the exception type. |
| 503 | `database_unavailable, database_error` | PostgreSQL cannot be reached or could not complete the request. Documented on every operation that uses the database; `Retry-After` is set. |

*Not found*

```http
GET /v1/compounds/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```

`HTTP 404`
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",

    "details": {

      "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"

  }
}

```

```json
}
```
